# @arki/kv

> A Redis key-value store and rate limiter for ARKI, built on Keyv and rate-limiter-flexible, with a Dot plugin and a Redis cache for HTTP idempotency. It is not a database and has no other backend than Redis.

A TTL on `KV` is seconds. A TTL on the idempotency cache is milliseconds.

## Import paths

<!-- llms:start -->
- `@arki/kv`: A Redis-backed key-value store and rate-limiter client (`KV`) with an in-memory fallback. `KV`, `createKV`, `createRateLimitKV`.
- `@arki/kv/env`: The validated KV and Redis environment variables (`KV_URL`, `RATE_LIMIT_REDIS_URL`, ...). `env`.
- `@arki/kv/errors`: `RateLimitExceededError` and the initialization error codes. `KVInitializationError`, `KV_INITIALIZATION_ERROR_CODES`, `RateLimitExceededError`.
- `@arki/kv/instance`: Lazy-singleton helpers that build a `KV` from the environment. `createKVInstance`, `initializeKV`, `kv`.
- `@arki/kv/redis/idempotency`: The HTTP response cache on Redis: `@arki/http/idempotency` stores a finished response here and replays it when the same `Idempotency-Key` comes again. `redisResponseCache`; types `RedisResponseCacheOptions`.
- `@arki/kv/dot`: DOT adapter for @arki/kv. `KV_PLUGIN_ERROR_CODES`, `kv`; types `KvDotOptions`, `KvServices`.
<!-- llms:end -->

## Rules that bite

- `set` takes seconds. The idempotency cache takes milliseconds.
- The memory fallback is per process. It does not share counts between instances.
- Hold the limiter returned by `getRateLimiter`. Each call serialises the options.
- `kv.optional()` can give `null`. Handle it in every consumer.
- Match on `error.code`, never on the message.
